description: Execution PRD for 58 open GitHub issues from PR #4 red team security review and PR #8 defensive architecture review. Triaged into 49 atomic stories across 4 gates.

stories.title: Wire sender key encryption into envelope seal/open pipeline
stories.description: The envelope seal/open path goes directly from inner envelope to MLS encryption, skipping the sender key AES-256-GCM layer specified in ADR-002. The sender key module is fully implemented but not wired into the envelope pipeline. This means the per-sender forward secrecy layer is absent.
acceptanceCriteria: seal_envelope() applies encrypt_sender_layer() to the serialized inner envelope bytes BEFORE passing them to MLS encrypt()
open_envelope() applies decrypt_sender_layer() to the MLS-decrypted bytes BEFORE deserializing the inner envelope
seal_envelope() accepts a SenderKey parameter for the sender's current sender key
open_envelope() accepts a SenderKey parameter for the sender's current sender key
Existing seal/open roundtrip tests pass with sender key layer integrated
New test confirms that ciphertext produced by seal_envelope cannot be opened without the correct sender key even if MLS decryption succeeds
New test confirms tampered sender-key ciphertext is rejected with SenderKeyError::AuthenticationFailed before inner envelope deserialization is attempted
actionItems: Add SenderKey import from crate::crypto::sender_keys to outer.rs
Modify seal_envelope() signature to accept sender_key: &SenderKey parameter
In seal_envelope(), after serializing inner envelope, insert sender key encryption step before MLS encrypt()
Pass the sender-key-encrypted bytes (not raw serialized bytes) to MLS encrypt()
Modify open_envelope() signature to accept sender_key: &SenderKey parameter
In open_envelope(), after MLS decrypt, insert sender key decryption step before deserializing inner envelope
Add EnvelopeError variants for sender key encryption/decryption failures
Update all existing seal/open tests to pass a SenderKey to both functions
Add test: seal with sender key A, attempt open with sender key B — must fail

details.currentPipeline: seal: serialize(inner) -> MLS_encrypt -> outer | open: MLS_decrypt -> deserialize(inner) -> verify
details.correctPipeline: seal: serialize(inner) -> sender_key_encrypt -> MLS_encrypt -> outer | open: MLS_decrypt -> sender_key_decrypt -> deserialize(inner) -> verify
details.adrReference: ADR-002 specifies the sender-side AES-256-GCM key layer between serialization and MLS encryption. ADR-007 specifies the pull-based sender key distribution protocol.

stories.result: Already implemented in previous iteration. Sender key layer wired into seal_envelope/open_envelope. Verified and committed.

stories.title: Fix finalize_close key destruction ordering
stories.description: `finalize_close` destroys cryptographic keys before verifying the state transition from `Closing` to `Closed` is valid. If the transition fails, key material is already irreversibly destroyed.
acceptanceCriteria: finalize_close() validates the Closing -> Closed state transition BEFORE destroying any key material
If the state transition validation fails, no key material is destroyed and the original error is returned
If key destruction fails after a successful state transition, the error is returned and the context state reflects the failure
New test confirms that calling finalize_close() on a context not in Closing state returns an error AND does not destroy keys
New test confirms that calling finalize_close() on a Closing context succeeds and destroys keys in the correct order
actionItems: In finalize_close(), move the state transition validation to execute BEFORE the key destruction call
Add guard clause returning ContextError if current state is not Closing
Only after state transition is validated, proceed to key destruction
Add test: call finalize_close() on Active context — must return error, keys intact
Add test: call finalize_close() on Closing context — must succeed, keys destroyed

details.currentOrdering: 1. Destroy keys 2. Validate state transition 3. Emit event
details.correctOrdering: 1. Validate state transition 2. Destroy keys 3. Emit event
details.irreversibility: Key destruction is irreversible — once zeroized, encrypted content becomes permanently unreadable.

stories.title: Guard OpenMLS decrypt against panic DoS
stories.description: OpenMLS panics on AEAD decryption failure for tampered ciphertexts (test uses #[should_panic]). A malicious relay can send crafted ciphertext that crashes the client process. Should wrap in catch_unwind() or handle the error path.
acceptanceCriteria: decrypt() in mls/encrypt.rs wraps the OpenMLS process_message() call in std::panic::catch_unwind()
A panic from OpenMLS during decryption is converted to MlsError::DecryptionFailed
The existing #[should_panic] test is converted to a normal error-checking test
New test confirms crafted ciphertext with tampered AEAD tag returns MlsError::DecryptionFailed instead of panicking
After a caught panic, subsequent encrypt/decrypt operations on the same group still work correctly
actionItems: Wrap group.group.process_message() in std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(|| { ... }))
Map caught panics to MlsError::DecryptionFailed
Update open_envelope_rejects_tampered_encrypted_blob test: remove #[should_panic], assert Err
Add dedicated tampered ciphertext test in mls/encrypt.rs
Verify group consistency after caught panic

details.attackVector: Malicious relay sends crafted ciphertext that crashes client process via panic, achieving denial of service.

stories.title: Add MCP authorization (context membership + UCAN on reads)
stories.description: (1) handle_tools_call validates UCAN capability but does not check active_context_ids() to verify the agent is a member of the target context. A crafted tool call with a known context ID could invoke tools cross-context. (2) handle_resources_read performs NO UCAN capability validation after initialization. It checks active_context_ids() (context existence) but any initialized client can read any context's members, events, and tools without authorization.
acceptanceCriteria: handle_tools_call() checks caller DID membership in target context BEFORE executing the tool
handle_tools_call() returns JSON-RPC error if membership check fails
handle_resources_read() validates UCAN capability for the requested resource type before returning data
handle_resources_read() returns JSON-RPC error if UCAN validation fails
New test: tools/call with valid UCAN but caller not a member returns membership error
New test: resources/read without valid UCAN returns authorization error
New test: resources/read with valid UCAN and membership succeeds
actionItems: In handle_tools_call(), add membership check via active_context_ids() after parsing context_id
In handle_resources_read(), add UCAN capability validation matching resource type
Return JsonRpcResponse::error with code -32603 for authorization failures
Add unit tests using mock ContextProvider

details.handleToolsCallGap: Validates UCAN but never checks active_context_ids()
details.handleResourcesReadGap: Zero authorization checks after MCP initialization
details.partiallyFixed: Issue #18 pre-initialization bypass already fixed via commit 8f35edd in PR #8. handle_request now rejects all methods except initialize and ping before initialization. Only the missing UCAN authorization on resource reads remains unfixed.
details.existingChecks: handle_resources_read already checks active_context_ids() for context existence — only UCAN capability validation is missing. Do not re-implement the existence check.

stories.result: Added context membership check to handle_tools_call and UCAN capability validation to handle_resources_read. 3 new tests, all 158 scp-mcp tests pass.

stories.title: Add authorization check to leave_context
stories.description: `ContextManager::leave_context()` checks `ContextState::Active` but never validates that the caller is the member being removed or has `MemberRemove` capability. An observer (lowest-privilege role) can remove the admin.
acceptanceCriteria: leave_context() validates caller_did == member_did (self-removal) OR caller holds MemberRemove capability
leave_context() returns ContextError if neither condition is met
Observer role cannot remove admin via leave_context()
Admin with MemberRemove can remove any member
Member can always self-remove regardless of role
New test: observer calls leave_context with admin's DID — returns authorization error
New test: admin calls leave_context with observer's DID — succeeds
New test: member calls leave_context with own DID — succeeds
actionItems: Add caller_did parameter to leave_context()
Check if caller_did == member_did; if so, allow (self-removal)
If not self-removal, check MemberRemove capability via ContextRoleState
Return ContextError::Unauthorized if neither condition met
Add unit tests for all authorization scenarios

details.attackScenario: Observer calls leave_context with admin's DID. Admin removed. In bilateral context, this destroys the context.

stories.title: Replace ContextManager std::sync::Mutex with tokio + atomic state ops
stories.description: (1) ContextManager uses std::sync::Mutex instead of tokio::sync::Mutex. Violates .docs/standards/rust.md line 29. Risks deadlocks when MutexGuard held across .await points. Panic poisons mutex, bricking entire manager. (2) All ContextManager operations check state then perform mutation in separate steps — TOCTOU race.
acceptanceCriteria: ContextManager uses tokio::sync::Mutex for all internal state
No std::sync::Mutex remains in ContextManager
All state-check-then-mutate sequences are atomic within a single lock acquisition
create_context, join_context, leave_context, send_message, close_context all operate atomically
A panic in one operation does not poison the mutex
No MutexGuard is held across any .await point
All existing ContextManager tests pass
actionItems: Replace use std::sync::Mutex with tokio::sync::Mutex in manager.rs
Convert .lock().map_err(|_| ...) to .lock().await (tokio Mutex has no poisoning)
Restructure each method: acquire lock -> check state -> mutate -> release, all in one scope
Ensure no .await calls while holding MutexGuard
Remove PoisonError handling
Add concurrent operations test
Add panic-recovery test

details.stdMutexRisks: Deadlock across .await, poisoning on panic, violates standards
details.tocTouRace: lock -> check Active -> unlock -> lock -> mutate: state can change between steps

stories.result: Replaced std::sync::Mutex with tokio::sync::Mutex. Atomic state-check-then-mutate. try_read_state() for sync checks. All 1385 scp-core tests pass.

stories.title: Fix ContextManager TTL expiry key destruction and event logging
stories.description: The manager's TTL timer implementation skips key destruction and event logging that the standalone TtlTimer::spawn performs. When the manager's timer fires on context expiry, crypto state is not destroyed and no ContextExpired event is logged.
acceptanceCriteria: TTL timer fires key destruction via KeyDestructionOrchestrator
TTL timer logs ContextExpired event to the event log
Ephemeral contexts: key material zeroized and MLS group destroyed on TTL expiry
Summary contexts: verification window opened before key destruction
Full contexts: no key destruction, only expiry event logged
New test: ephemeral context with short TTL — verify keys destroyed after expiry
New test: verify ContextExpired event in event log after TTL expiry
actionItems: Add key destruction dispatch to TTL expiry handler
Add ContextExpired event emission to TTL expiry handler
Ephemeral: call destroy_group() and zeroize sender keys
Summary: open SummaryVerificationWindow before key destruction
Full: skip key destruction, only log event
Add integration tests with short TTL contexts

details.securityImpact: For ephemeral contexts, TTL expiry through the manager leaves keys intact — violating the ephemeral guarantee.

stories.title: Add relay server DoS protections
stories.description: No rate limiting on any relay server operation. InMemoryBlobStorage has no capacity limit. Subscription limit is per-connection (100) but no connection limit per IP. deliver_to_subscribers uses try_send which silently drops on full channel. Cleanup path acquires write lock on SubscriptionRegistry, creating lock contention DoS vector.
acceptanceCriteria: RelayConfig includes max_connections_per_ip (default: 10)
RelayConfig includes max_total_connections (default: 1000)
RelayConfig includes rate_limit_publishes_per_second (default: 100 per IP)
InMemoryBlobStorage enforces max_blobs capacity limit (default: 100_000)
Connections exceeding limits are rejected
Publish operations exceeding rate limits return error
deliver_to_subscribers logs warning when try_send fails
Cleanup path minimizes write lock duration
New tests for all limit enforcements
actionItems: Add rate limiting and connection limit fields to RelayConfig
Add per-IP connection counter to RelayServer
Implement token-bucket rate limiter for publish operations
Add max_blobs to InMemoryBlobStorage
Add tracing::warn!() for try_send failures
Refactor cleanup: read-lock scan, brief write-lock removal
Add tests for all limits

details.currentState: Zero DoS protections. Unlimited connections, unlimited blob storage, no rate limiting.

stories.result: Added per-IP connection limits, total connection cap, token-bucket rate limiter, blob storage capacity, tracing warnings, optimized cleanup locking. 22 server + 16 storage tests pass.

stories.title: Bound epoch grace store and trigger MLS key destruction
stories.description: (1) EpochGraceStore in crypto/mls/epoch_grace.rs has no maximum capacity. add_epoch adds to a HashMap with no size bound. expire_old_epochs must be called explicitly — it is not called from add_epoch. An attacker who can trigger frequent epoch advances can accumulate unbounded grace entries. (2) expire_old_epochs removes HashMap entries but does not trigger actual MLS key material deletion in OpenMLS. See also: #24 (BLACK-008) covers the unbounded growth aspect; #32 tracks the distinct key destruction gap.
acceptanceCriteria: EpochGraceStore enforces maximum capacity (e.g., 100 epochs)
add_epoch() calls expire_old_epochs() before inserting
When an epoch is expired, corresponding MLS key material is destroyed
expire_old_epochs() returns list of expired epoch numbers
New test: exceed max_capacity, verify store never exceeds limit
New test: key material for expired epoch is deleted from MLS provider
Forward secrecy: after grace window closes, old epoch messages cannot be decrypted
Verify whether OpenMLS retains key material for epochs tracked by EpochGraceStore and document findings
actionItems: Add MAX_GRACE_EPOCHS constant (100) and max_capacity field
Modify add_epoch() to call expire_old_epochs() at start
After purge, if still at capacity, evict oldest epoch
Change expire_old_epochs() return type to Vec<u64>
Add key destruction callback for expired epochs
In caller site, call OpenMLS delete_epoch_key_material for each expired epoch
Add capacity and key destruction tests

details.keyMaterialLeak: expire_old_epochs only removes HashMap entries, not actual OpenMLS key material. Forward secrecy violated.
details.openmlsKeyRetention: Nuance: The store tracks which epochs are in grace, but actual cryptographic key material is managed by OpenMLS internally. The attack's impact depends on whether OpenMLS retains key material for epochs listed in the grace store. Verify OpenMLS behavior before assuming key material persists.
details.attackVector: An attacker who can trigger frequent epoch advances can accumulate unbounded grace entries, extending the forward secrecy window.

stories.result: Added MAX_GRACE_EPOCHS capacity (100), auto-expire on add, OnEpochExpired callback, oldest-epoch eviction. Forward secrecy tests added. Documented OpenMLS key lifecycle.

stories.title: Complete equivocation defenses (suppression tracker wiring)
stories.description: (1) Selective message suppression unfixed — deliver_to_subscribers uses try_send — if the channel is full, the message is silently dropped. A relay that artificially fills a target's buffer causes selective drops. (2) Checkpoint delivery circularity (partially fixed) — ConsistencyCheckpoint is sent as regular MLS messages through the relay. A compromised relay can suppress checkpoints. Fix commit fbc2256 in PR #8 adds checkpoint signature verification but does not address the delivery channel circularity. (3) SuppressionTracker has the data structures for cross-relay comparison (per-blob, per-adapter delivery sets) but the integration in TransportManager.subscribe_context is not fully wired. record_delivery is not called from subscription delivery paths.
acceptanceCriteria: TransportManager calls SuppressionTracker::record_delivery() for every envelope received from each adapter
TransportManager periodically calls check_suppressions() and emits warnings
Suppression warnings downgrade flagged relay's ReliabilityScore
deliver_to_subscribers tracks failed sends instead of silent drop
New test: two adapters receive same blob, no warning
New test: one adapter receives, other does not within window, warning emitted
New test: warning triggers reliability score downgrade
SuppressionTracker is bounded with LRU eviction
actionItems: In MergedSubscriptionStream::poll_next(), call record_delivery() after dedup
Add periodic check_suppressions() call in TransportManager
Emit TransportEvent::SuppressionDetected for warnings
Update relay scores on suppression detection
Track try_send failures in server.rs
Add SuppressionTracker capacity bounds (10,000 entries)
Add integration tests for full flow

details.suppressionTrackerState: SuppressionTracker in scoring.rs tracks per-blob, per-adapter delivery sets for cross-relay comparison (more capable than originally stated), but requires record_delivery() to be called by the client — wiring is incomplete.
details.partiallyFixed: Issue #21 checkpoint signature verification already implemented via commit fbc2256 in PR #8. Only selective suppression and delivery channel circularity remain unfixed. Do not re-implement checkpoint signatures.
details.attackMechanism: A relay that artificially fills a target's channel buffer causes selective message drops.
details.wiringLocation: Integration point is TransportManager.subscribe_context — SuppressionTracker.record_delivery() must be called from subscription delivery paths.

stories.title: Harden UCAN validation (restrict stateless, fix clock)
stories.description: (1) validate_ucan_stateless() at validate.rs:473 is pub and skips steps 3 (chain), 7 (attenuation), 9 (nonce), and 10 (revocation). Only used in tests but accessible to downstream. Should be pub(crate) or removed. (2) unwrap_or_default() returning Duration::ZERO on pre-epoch systems allows timestamp bypass.
acceptanceCriteria: validate_ucan_stateless() is no longer reachable from outside scp-core (pub(crate) or removed)

All existing tests pass

Replace unwrap_or_default() with Result-returning helper propagating ClockError
Add ClockError variant to UCAN validation error enum
Add unit tests for clock failure and visibility restriction

stories.title: Add domain separation prefix to canonical hash
stories.description: compute_canonical_hash() in inner.rs has no domain separator (e.g., "SCP-INNER-ENVELOPE-V1:"). Same Ed25519 key used for multiple purposes, enabling cross-protocol signature confusion. PR #8 added length prefixes for variable-length fields but NOT a domain separator.
acceptanceCriteria: compute_canonical_hash() prepends a fixed domain separator before hashing
Domain separator is documented as a constant
Unit test: hash output changes when domain separator is altered
All existing tests pass after updating expected hash values
actionItems: Define DOMAIN_SEPARATOR constant in inner.rs
Prepend domain separator to hasher input before any field data
Update all test fixtures depending on hash output
Add unit tests for domain separator inclusion

details.crossProtocolRisk: Ed25519 keys reused across signing contexts — envelope, UCAN, DID auth. Without domain separator, signature from one context could be valid in another.

stories.title: Switch Ed25519 to verify_strict()
stories.description: Ed25519 verification uses verify() instead of verify_strict(). Without strict verification, signatures with non-canonical S values are accepted, enabling signature malleability attacks.
acceptanceCriteria: All Ed25519 verify() calls replaced with verify_strict() in all three files
Unit test in each module: signature with non-canonical S value is rejected
No verify() calls remain for Ed25519 in signing/verification paths
All existing tests pass
actionItems: Replace .verify( with .verify_strict( in dht.rs, inner.rs, validate.rs
Add test per module: non-canonical S signature rejected
Grep codebase to confirm no non-strict calls remain

details.malleability: For any valid (R, S), (R, L-S) is also valid. verify_strict() rejects non-canonical S values.

stories.title: Fix DID AtomicU64 to AcqRel ordering
stories.description: DID document sequence number uses Ordering::Relaxed which provides no synchronization guarantees across threads. Should use AcqRel to ensure correct happens-before ordering.
acceptanceCriteria: All AtomicU64 loads use Ordering::Acquire, stores use Release, RMW uses AcqRel
No Ordering::Relaxed on sequence number atomic
Concurrent test: N threads calling fetch_add produce unique monotonic values
All existing tests pass
actionItems: Replace Relaxed with Acquire on loads, Release on stores, AcqRel on fetch_add/compare_exchange
Add concurrent monotonicity test

stories.title: Resolve sender key internally in open_envelope
stories.description: ADR-002 specifies that open_envelope should resolve the sender public key internally from the MLS group state. Current implementation requires caller to provide it, creating opportunity to supply wrong key.
acceptanceCriteria: open_envelope no longer accepts sender public key from caller
open_envelope resolves sender key internally from MLS group state
Test: envelope from valid group member decrypted with internally resolved key
Test: sender_id not in group returns UnknownSender error
All existing tests pass after updating call sites
actionItems: Modify open_envelope to accept MLS group state instead of explicit key
Implement internal sender key resolution from outer envelope header
Return UnknownSender error if sender not in group

stories.title: Zeroize MLS crypto state in destroy_group
stories.description: destroy_group sets a boolean flag but does not actively zeroize the MLS group's cryptographic state in memory. Key material persists until garbage collected.
acceptanceCriteria: destroy_group zeroizes all cryptographic key material before setting destroyed flag
zeroize crate used for all sensitive fields
After destroy_group, encrypt/decrypt returns GroupDestroyed error
All existing tests pass

details.exposureWindow: Without zeroization, key material persists until garbage collected (in Rust: until the owning struct is dropped/deallocated). Recoverable via core dump, cold boot, or swap.

stories.title: Add replay protection to sender key and block notification protocols
stories.description: (1) SenderKeyRequest messages have no nonce or timestamp. A captured request can be replayed to obtain sender keys. (2) Block notifications carry a timestamp but it is not validated for freshness. A delayed or replayed block notification is accepted regardless of age.
acceptanceCriteria: SenderKeyRequest includes cryptographic nonce (16+ bytes) and timestamp
SenderKeyResponse echoes request nonce for binding
Duplicate nonces within 5-minute window rejected
Block notification timestamps validated for freshness (30s threshold)

Add nonce echo to SenderKeyResponse
Implement bounded nonce cache
Add freshness validation to block notification handler
Add replay and freshness tests

stories.title: Make UCAN revocation atomic with propagation bounding
stories.description: (1) revoke_ucan adds CID to local revocation list (step 2), then attempts distribution (step 3). If distribution fails, local mutation is not rolled back — split-brain. (2) Between local revocation and MLS distribution completing, revoked tokens remain valid on some members. No mechanism exists for the revoker to confirm propagation or for members to refuse operations during the window.
acceptanceCriteria: revoke_ucan is transactional: failed distribution rolls back local revocation
RevocationPending intermediate state marks token during propagation
After successful distribution, state transitions to Revoked

Tests: failed distribution rolls back, successful distribution commits, RevocationPending denies capability
actionItems: Add RevocationPending state
Refactor: mark pending -> distribute -> commit on success / rollback on failure
Treat RevocationPending as revoked for capability checks
Add confirmation event for successful distribution
Add tests for all scenarios

details.splitBrain: If distribution fails, revoker thinks token revoked but no one else does. Persists until next successful distribution.

stories.title: Add capacity limits to nonce tracker
stories.description: InMemoryNonceTracker in validate.rs: Unbounded HashMap, no pruning, no capacity limit. Used in tests but is pub. Production NonceTracker<C> in nonce.rs: Has pruning every 1000 checks or 10 minutes, and is per-context scoped. However, it has no capacity limit, and pruning is O(n) via HashMap::retain. The 24-hour minimum retention at high nonce rates could consume significant memory. Cross-context isolation: InMemoryNonceTracker is NOT per-context while production NonceTracker<C> IS per-context — valid concern for test/Phase 2 usage.
acceptanceCriteria: Production NonceTracker has configurable max_capacity (default: 100,000)
Exceeding max_capacity returns NonceTrackerFull error
InMemoryNonceTracker restricted to #[cfg(test)] or gains capacity limit
O(n) HashMap::retain pruning latency addressed: either replaced with an O(1)-amortized structure or benchmarked and documented as acceptable at max_capacity
Tests: capacity exceeded rejects, pruning allows acceptance again
InMemoryNonceTracker either restricted to #[cfg(test)] or made per-context scoped to match production NonceTracker
actionItems: Add max_capacity field to NonceTracker (default 100,000)
In check_and_record(), check capacity before insert; attempt prune if full
Return NonceTrackerFull error if still at capacity after prune
Restrict InMemoryNonceTracker visibility or add capacity
Add tests

details.memoryCalculation: 100 nonces/sec * 86400s retention * ~100 bytes = ~864 MB per context
details.inMemoryTracker: InMemoryNonceTracker in validate.rs: Unbounded HashMap, no pruning, no capacity limit. Used in tests but is pub.
details.productionTracker: Production NonceTracker<C> in nonce.rs: Has pruning every 1000 checks or 10 minutes, and is per-context scoped. However, it has no capacity limit, and pruning is O(n) via HashMap::retain. The 24-hour minimum retention at high nonce rates could consume significant memory.
details.crossContextIsolation: InMemoryNonceTracker is NOT per-context while production NonceTracker<C> IS per-context — valid concern for test/Phase 2 usage.
details.pruningComplexity: HashMap::retain is O(n) — at 8.6M entries this creates noticeable latency spikes

stories.title: Fix UCAN validation (nbf > exp check + CID format)
stories.description: (1) UCAN token validation does not check that nbf (not before) is less than exp (expiry). A token with nbf > exp is inherently invalid but is not rejected. stories.title: Optimize SenderKeyStore (Cow return + epoch overflow)
stories.description: (1) Each key lookup in SenderKeyStore performs a heap allocation. For high-throughput message decryption, this creates unnecessary allocation pressure. Epoch increment uses checked_add, returns EpochOverflow on overflow
Tests: lookup doesn't allocate for cached key, epoch at MAX returns error
actionItems: Change lookup return type to Cow/reference

Add EpochOverflow error variant
Add tests

stories.title: Design Sybil-resistant blocking mechanism
stories.description: handle_sender_key_request in crypto/sender_keys/key_protocol.rs checks block_list.contains(&request.requester_did) — per-DID blocking only. A Sybil identity (new DID controlled by the same actor) not in the block list can request and receive the new sender key. The protocol tenet "every agent traces to a human DID" is not mechanically enforced. Classification: Architectural. Requires identity-level (not DID-level) blocking or external Sybil resistance.

stories.title: Design pseudonym rotation for traffic analysis resistance
stories.description: Pseudonym derivation in envelope/pseudonym.rs is HMAC-SHA256(identity_key_material, context_id || "scp-pseudonym") — deterministic, never rotated. The relay sees routing_id and recipient_hint on every envelope. deliver_to_subscribers delivers blobs by routing_id with no delay/batching, making timing correlation trivial. Cross-relay fanout sends identical envelopes simultaneously. Classification: Architectural (P2/defense-in-depth). Requires pseudonym rotation or traffic analysis resistance mechanisms.
